prompt_text: What is the best Airbnb or short term rental to book in Nashville for a family of four?
answer_verbatim:
I can help you find the best short‑term rental — I just need a few details to make concrete recommendations. Quick guidance now plus what I’ll need if you want me to pull specific listings:

Top neighborhoods for a family of four
- 12 South — charming, walkable, family‑friendly restaurants/parks; easy access to the rest of the city. Good for a bungalow or 2‑BR house.
- Germantown — quieter, historic, good restaurants, close to downtown and the riverfront. Lots of modern condos and 2‑3 bedroom townhomes.
- East Nashville — artsy, residential, many houses with yards. Great for kids and families who want a neighborhood feel.
- West End / Hillsboro Village — near Centennial Park and Vanderbilt/Parthenon; good if you want museums and green space walkable.
- The Gulch / Downtown — most central for attractions and Broadway, but louder and more nightlife‑oriented; get a full condo on a quiet floor if you go this route.

What to look for in a family rental
- Entire place (no shared rooms) with at least 2 bedrooms, or 1 BR + reliable sofa bed.
- Amenities: full kitchen, washer/dryer, high chair/pack‑n‑play (filter “family/kid friendly”), fenced yard or safe outdoor play area if you need it.
- Parking or easy street parking if you’ll rent a car.
- Quiet street or upper floor unit if near downtown nightlife.
- Superhost or hosts with many recent 5‑star reviews and fast response.
- Flexible cancellation policy if plans might change.
- Clear house rules about noise/pets and any additional fees.

Budget and timing (ballpark)
- Midrange 2‑BR houses/condos in family neighborhoods: expect roughly $150–$350/night depending on season.
- Downtown/Gulch luxury condos or historic homes: $250–$600+/night.
- Peak times (March conventions, CMA Fest, major events) push prices and reduce availability — book early.

Safety and convenience tips
- Read recent reviews for noise and cleanliness.
- Check exact address area on a map for proximity to grocery stores, parks, hospitals.
- Watch fees (cleaning, service, extra guest fees) — total price can be much higher than the nightly rate.
- If traveling without a car, prioritize walkability and transit access.

If you want specific listing recommendations
Tell me:
- Exact dates (or date range)
- Budget per night or total
- Any must‑have amenities (crib, fenced yard, garage, number of beds)
- Kids’ ages and whether you’ll have a car
- Preferred neighborhoods (or “walkable to Broadway” / “quiet family area”)

With that I’ll suggest 4–6 specific rental types/areas and what to search for (I can’t pull live bookings directly, but I’ll give listing title keywords and filters to use to find the best matches).
